title: Zero Trust Exchange for B2B: site-to-site, partner and B2C access to private applications

prose.text: {{b2b-what}} {{b2b-vs-zpa}} How B2B differs from standard ZPA is open {{gap:b2b-zpa-contrast}}.
The ZPA federation feature with a similar name is in [[zpa.b2b-federation]].

Whether B2B handles identity and trust across organizations, and not only across segments of one organization, is open {{gap:b2b-cross-org}}. {{b2b-sdk-class}} Whether that is the B2B surface, distinct from ZPA, is open {{gap:b2b-sdk}}.

checks.do: For a question about partner or B2C access, check whether the scenario is site-to-site, partner portal or B2C mobile before answering from the solution-details claim.

b2b-sdk-class.statement: The vendored Python SDK defines a ZPA TenantFederationProvisioningAPI class.

b2b-what.statement: The Zscaler B2B page says B2B is a cloud service that gives business customers secure and fast access to B2B applications; its solution details are site-to-site B2B connectivity based on zero trust network access (ZTNA), B2B partner portal access and B2C mobile app access.

quotes: Zscaler B2B is a cloud service that gives your business customers secure and fast access to B2B applications.

Solution Details
Site-to-site B2B connectivity
B2B partner portal access
B2C mobile app access

Site-to-site connectivity based on zero trust network access (ZTNA) enables secure access to private B2B apps by establishing connectivity between locations on a dynamic identity- and context-aware basis.

b2b-vs-zpa.statement: The page says zero trust network access limits partner access to only authorized private applications, without putting partners on the network, and delivers visibility into all partner activity down to the user, device and named app level; browser-based access lets partners reach authorized applications from any location, on any device.

quotes: Zero trust network access limits partner access to only authorized private applications, without putting them on the network, and delivers comprehensive visibility into all partner activity down to the user, device, and named app level.
Browser-based access enables partners to seamlessly and securely access authorized applications from any location, on any device.

b2b-no-inbound.statement: The page says Zscaler B2B provides site-to-site connectivity without requiring inbound DMZs and open ports, that it hides B2B apps from the internet, and that a direct-to-cloud architecture eliminates complex site-to-site VPNs or hub-and-spoke networks.

quotes: It provides site-to-site connectivity to support business partners and third parties around the globe, on any device, without requiring inbound DMZs and open ports that create an attack surface.

Minimize the attack surface
Hide your B2B apps from the internet
Eliminate complex site-to-site VPNs or hub-and-spoke networks with a direct-to-cloud architecture that improves application performance.

b2b-inspection.statement: The page says Zscaler's proxy architecture, built on the principle of least privilege, enables full TLS/SSL inspection at scale, with connections brokered between users and applications based on identity, context and business policies.

quotes: Built on the principle of least privilege, Zscaler’s proxy architecture enables full TLS/SSL inspection at scale, with connections brokered between users and applications based on identity, context, and business policies.

b2b-cross-org.title: Whether B2B handles cross-organization identity and trust
b2b-cross-org.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Distinguishing detail vs base ZPA: B2B handles cross-organization identity and trust, not just cross-segment-within-one-org.' The B2B capture describes identity- and context-aware access for external parties but does not describe cross-organization trust.

b2b-sdk.title: Whether Zscaler B2B has an SDK surface distinct from ZPA
b2b-sdk.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'No SDK distinct from ZPA's; configured via the broader ZPA admin surfaces.' The B2B capture names no API or SDK surface. The vendored Python SDK does have a ZPA TenantFederationProvisioningAPI (b2b-sdk-class), but whether it is the ZTE-for-B2B surface is not captured.

b2b-zpa-contrast.title: How Zscaler B2B differs from standard ZPA
b2b-zpa-contrast.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the earlier non-verbatim capture of the Zscaler B2B page said standard ZPA is user-to-application access (north-south, single-org) while B2B gives external parties secure access to private B2B apps without network exposure. The current page does not mention ZPA.
